title: Moving Averages
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/0/bo: A **moving average** averages the closing prices of the last few candles and draws them as a smooth line on the chart. That filters out the small wiggles, so the **overall price direction** is easier to see.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/1/bo: **SMA (simple moving average)** means adding up the closes of the last N candles and dividing by N. Each new candle pushes the oldest one out, which is why it's called **moving**.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/2/pr: Here are Bitcoin's last three closes. What's the 3-candle SMA?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/2/ex: (60,000 + 61,200 + 62,400) ÷ 3 = 61,200. The sum alone isn't enough; you have to divide by the number of candles.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/3/st: A 50-candle moving average reacts to price changes faster than a 10-candle one.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/3/ex: In an SMA 50, each new candle carries only 1/50 of the weight; in an SMA 10 it's 1/10. So the 50 is slower and smoother.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/4/bo: A moving average is built from past prices, so it always follows price **with a delay (lag)**. Short periods are faster; long periods are smoother but slower. **20, 50 and 200** are the most popular periods.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/4/ti: Price above a rising MA means buyers have the upper hand. Below a falling MA, it's the opposite.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/5/pr: What does price's position relative to the MA tell you?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/5/ex: Almost every candle closed below the line, and the MA itself points down. Sellers are in control.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/6/pr: Tap the first candle that closed above the moving average.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/6/ex: Before this candle, every close was below the gold line. This strong green candle closed above the MA: the first sign that sellers are weakening, but not yet a confirmed uptrend.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/7/se: The ___ the MA period, the smoother its line, but the more ___ it has.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/7/ex: A long MA filters out more noise, but it reacts later when the trend changes.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l1/steps/8/pa: The MA line trailing behind price
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/0/bo: An **EMA (exponential moving average)** gives **more weight to recent candles**. So compared with an SMA of the same period, it **reacts to price changes sooner** and stays closer to price after sharp moves.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/0/ti: In this course, the lines you see on the charts are SMAs. You'll learn the EMA with numbers and examples.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/1/bo: First work out the weighting factor: **k = 2 ÷ (N + 1)**. Then for each candle: **new EMA = previous EMA + k × (close − previous EMA)**. So each time, the EMA closes only part of the gap to the new price.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/2/pr: What's the weighting factor (k) for an EMA 19?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/2/ex: k = 2 ÷ (19 + 1) = 2 ÷ 20 = 0.1. So each new candle closes 10% of the gap between the EMA and price.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/3/st: After a price reversal, the EMA 50 usually changes direction sooner than the SMA 50.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/3/ex: With the same period, the EMA gives more weight to fresh candles, so it turns sooner after a reversal. That same speed also creates more false signals.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/4/pr: The gold line is the SMA 10. If you added the EMA 10 to this chart, where would it sit on the last candle?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/4/op: Above the gold line, closer to price
Below the gold line, farther from price
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/4/ex: After this sharp jump, the EMA rises faster because it weights fresh candles more, so it sits between the SMA and price. It still trails price, though.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/5/bo: Neither is always better; it's a trade-off between **speed and noise**. The EMA signals sooner but also gives more **false signals**. The SMA is calmer and widely used for the **long-term trend** (like the 200-day). Many short-term traders use the EMA 9 and 21.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/5/ti: Pick one setting and stick with it. Constantly switching settings just confuses you.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/6/pr: Ethereum's EMA 9 was $3,000 yesterday, and today price closed at $3,100. What's today's EMA 9?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/6/ex: 3,000 + 0.2 × (3,100 − 3,000) = 3,020. The EMA only moves 20% of the gap, not all of it.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/7/pr: Sort these moving averages from fastest to slowest.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/7/ex: Shorter periods are faster, and with the same period, the EMA reacts to price changes sooner than the SMA.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l2/steps/8/pa: The new candle's share in the EMA
A signal price soon moves against
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/0/bo: In an uptrend, price often pulls back to near a moving average and bounces from there. Because this line moves along with price, it's called **dynamic support**. In a downtrend, the same line plays the role of **dynamic resistance**.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/1/ti: A zone, not an exact line
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/1/bo: Price doesn't always bounce exactly on the MA; sometimes it pokes through a little. Treat the MA as **a zone** and wait for a **confirmation candle**, like a hammer or a bullish engulfing. An MA is worth watching when the market has **respected it before**.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/1/ti: Dynamic support only makes sense when the MA is rising. A flat MA means there's no trend.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/2/pr: Tap the candle that touched the MA and bounced back up with a green body.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/2/ex: This candle's lower wick dipped below the MA, but it closed green and above the line. Buyers stepped in at dynamic support, and the trend carried on.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/3/pr: It's an uptrend, and price has pulled back to the MA with a hammer candle. What's next?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/3/ex: The MA is rising, price respected it, and the hammer shows buyers rejected the lows. The trend is more likely to continue (not guaranteed). A sensible stop loss goes below the hammer's low.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/4/pr: Bitcoin is in an uptrend, and price is pulling back to the 8-period moving average (the gold line). Place the line where dynamic support is right now.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/4/ex: The 8-candle MA is now around 64,425 (the average close of the last 8 candles), and price is about $400 above it. This line shifts with every candle, so treat it as a zone and wait for a confirmation candle on the line before entering.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/5/st: If price closes below a rising MA several candles in a row and the MA flattens out, the uptrend is probably weakening.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/5/ex: Dynamic support holds while price stays above the MA. Back-to-back closes below the line and a flattening slope signal a weakening trend or the start of a range.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/6/bo: If price **closes below the MA** for several candles and the MA's slope turns flat or negative, that line is no longer support and may flip to **dynamic resistance**. A flat MA that price keeps crossing means a **trendless market**.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/7/pr: It's a downtrend, and price has rallied up to the MA, forming a candle with a long upper wick (a pin bar). What do you do?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/7/ex: A falling MA acts as dynamic resistance. The long upper wick shows sellers pushed price back down from the line. The drop is more likely to continue; put your stop loss above this candle's high.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/8/pr: You bought at dynamic support. Where's the most sensible place for your stop loss?
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/8/op: Just below the confirmation candle's low and the MA
No need; the MA will hold
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/8/ex: Price can poke slightly through the MA and come back. A stop below the confirmation candle's low means you only exit when your idea is truly invalidated.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/9/pr: Put the steps of a dynamic support bounce trade in order.
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/9/it: Wait for a pullback to the MA
Spot a confirmation candle, like a hammer
Enter with a stop below the low
Take profit near the previous high
lessons/moving-averages-u1-l3/steps/9/ex: First the trend, then wait for price to reach the zone, then confirmation, and finally an entry with defined risk. Skipping any step raises your odds of a mistake.
